/**
 * Machine-notice classification for PR discussion collection (gh-808).
 *
 * The harness posts STATUS/ARMING notices to its own PRs through the machine
 * login — arming notices, park/park-clear notices, validation and re-run
 * reports, merge-conflict reports, rework/review result summaries, human
 * escalations. Those notices are NOT review feedback: feeding them into the
 * rework input as threads with reply targeting made the rework agent spend
 * its replies on boilerplate answers to the machine itself (live: fa PR
 * #1428 round 2 — 9 of 13 replies were boilerplate).
 *
 * This module is the SINGLE SOURCE OF TRUTH for recognizing those notices.
 * The discrimination cannot be authorship-based: in this harness the reviewer
 * identity IS the machine login (the review agent posts inline comments with
 * the same credentials that post the notices), so classification keys on the
 * exact marker each poster writes at the START of its comment body — anchored
 * prefix match, never fuzzy text matching. A reviewer comment that merely
 * QUOTES a notice (blockquote, mid-body mention) therefore never matches.
 *
 * Comment bodies rendered through commentMarkup start with a markdown heading
 * (`### ✅ Rework Completed`), so a leading heading prefix is stripped before
 * the marker comparison.
 *
 * Consumption: js/common/scm.js (GitHub provider fetchDiscussions) and
 * js/common/githubHelpers.js (string-arg fetchDiscussionsAndRawData) drop
 * matching conversations from rawThreads and the discussions markdown, so
 * pr_discussions_raw.json contains zero machine-notice entries (gh-808 AC1)
 * while real review threads pass through with their ids intact (AC2).
 */

// Exact body-start markers of every PR-level notice the harness posts, with
// the poster that owns each. Keep in sync with the posters — when the armer
// wording changes, the marker changes here with it.
var MACHINE_NOTICE_MARKERS = [
    // js/smAgent.js — arm_rework notice
    '🧵 Unresolved review threads — rework armed.',
    // js/smAgent.js — validation park + park-clear notices
    '🅿️ Validation red — PR parked',
    '🅿️→▶ validation_failed cleared',
    // js/smAgent.js — rerun_cancelled_checks notice
    '🔁 Cancelled required checks re-run',
    // js/smAgent.js — conflict_rework report
    '⚠️ Merge conflict with main',
    // js/smAgent.js — fail_validation reports (all wording variants)
    '⚠️ Validation CI went red on the head',
    // js/smAgent.js — guest-PR park notice + human escalation (#701 style)
    '🛑 validation_failed',
    '🛑 @',
    // js/pushReworkChanges.js — rework completion comments (h3 headings)
    '✅ Rework Completed',
    '⚠️ Rework Completed',
    '✅ Rework Analysis Completed',
    // js/pushReworkChanges.js — rework failure reports
    '❌ Rework CLI Failed',
    '❌ Rework Push Skipped',
    '❌ Rework Push Failed',
    '❌ Rework Quality Gate Failed',
    '❌ Rework Workflow Error',
    // js/pushReworkChanges.js — re-review skip notices (token guard)
    '✅ Rework finished.',
    '⚠️ Rework finished with',
    // js/pushReworkChanges.js — fix summary + gate warnings + untargeted replies
    '🔧 Rework Complete —',
    '⚠️ Non-blocking gate warnings',
    '✅ Addressed',
    // js/postPRReviewComments.js — review summary (h2 heading)
    '🔍 Automated PR Review Completed',
    // js/postTestReworkResults.js / js/storyTestAutomationRework.js — test rework summaries
    '🔧 Test Rework Complete —',
    '🔧 Story Test Rework Complete —'
];

// Bot accounts whose PR threads are informational by platform convention
// (CI status, dependency updates) — shared by both collection paths so the
// heuristic lives in exactly one place.
var BOT_AUTHORS = ['github-actions[bot]', 'dependabot[bot]', 'renovate[bot]', 'codecov[bot]'];

blocks.text:
# Copilot Instructions — dmtools-agents

## Architecture

This is a **generic agents repository** (typically used as a git submodule at `agents/` inside product repos). It orchestrates AI-driven Agile delivery via [dmtools](https://github.com/nicku/dmtools) — a Java tool that provides a GraalJS runtime for agent scripts.

### Execution model

1. **SM Agent** (`sm.json` → `js/smAgent.js`) runs on a cron schedule, queries Jira via JQL rules, and dispatches specialized agents by triggering GitHub Actions workflows.
2. **Agent configs** (root `*.json` files) define individual agent jobs. Three job types exist:
   - `Teammate` — CLI-based agent (prepares context → runs AI CLI → post-processes result)
   - `JSRunner` — pure GraalJS logic executed inside dmtools (no AI CLI)
   - `TestCasesGenerator` — dmtools-native job for test case generation
3. **Project config** lives in the target repo at `.dmtools/config.js`, never here. This repo stays project-agnostic.

### Key layers

| Layer | Location | Purpose |
|-------|----------|---------|
| SM rules | `sm.json`, `sm_merge.json` | JQL-based ticket routing |
| Agent configs | root `*.json` | Job definitions (type, params, actions) |
| JS runtime scripts | `js/` | Pre/post actions, orchestration logic |
| Shared helpers | `js/common/` | SCM abstraction, Jira helpers, PR logic |
| Config system | `js/configLoader.js` + `js/config.js` | Discovery, merging, defaults |
| Prompts | `prompts/` | Markdown entry prompts for CLI agents |
| Instructions | `instructions/` | Reusable instruction packs (review, dev, rework, platform, tracker, scm) |
| Setup scripts | `setup/` | Shell scripts for CI environment setup |

## GraalJS Constraints

All `js/` runtime code executes in **dmtools GraalJS**, not Node.js.

- Use `var` declarations and plain functions (no `let`/`const`, no arrow functions, no async/await, no template literals).
- No Node.js APIs: no `fs`, `path`, `process`, `Buffer`, `child_process`, no npm packages.
- No browser APIs: no `fetch`, `window`, `document`.
- Use dmtools globals: `jira_*`, `github_*`, `ado_*`, `file_read`, `file_write`, `cli_execute_command`.
- Local `require('./module.js')` works only for files within this repo.
- **Requires resolve by execution time** (gh-823): a require that runs while a module initializes (top level, top-level `try`/`if`) resolves **file-relative**; a require that runs **after init** (any lazy/deferred call into an exported function) resolves against the **main script's directory — the pack's `js/` root — exclusively**, and a file-relative hit is never tried. `dmtools compile` discovers the pack closure strictly file-relative. Therefore: **hoist every require to the top of the module — never require lazily.** A lazy sibling-flat spec from `js/common/` looks for `js/x.js` and reds the tick ("Failed to require module"), and a pack-root-relative spec (`./common/…`) authored from a nested file fails the pack build. (Worker-source strings are the one exception — they execute on fresh engines and are authored js-root-relative: `require('./common/smProvider.js')`.) The repo-wide pin in `js/unit-tests/test_packRequirePath.js` fails the suite on ANY deferred require in packed code; its `ALLOWED_DEFERRED` list carries exactly one deliberate entry — `writeSolutionAndDiagrams.js`'s cycle-breaking `require('./writeSolutionAndLabels.js')` (hoisting it would close the labels→diagrams cycle at load time) — don't add a second one.
- Keep data structures JSON-safe.

## Running Tests

Tests run **standalone** inside dmtools GraalJS via the custom test runner. The repo is independent — no parent repo or submodule mount needed.

```bash
# Run from the dmtools-agents repo root
cd dmtools-agents

# All tests
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json

# Single test suite
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_smAgent.json
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_configLoader.json
```

Each `run_*.json` specifies which test files to load. Tests use `loadModule()` with mock injection — see `js/unit-tests/testRunner.js` for the framework API (`test()`, `suite()`, `assert.*`, `loadModule()`, `makeRequire()`).

# gh-1061: Blocked-rework comment: thread dump drowns response.md, and null-id machine notices make the gh-957 coverage gate unsatisfiable (live: dart gh-395 week-long loop)

## Description

## Goal — blocked-rework comment delivers the agent's message, not a thread dump (v1)

One sentence: **the blocked-rework PR comment becomes the agent's response.md** — the thread-coverage evidence moves to a folded appendix.

Today `handleReworkBlocked` (js/pushReworkChanges.js) composes one PR comment that leads with every unaddressed review thread inline-quoted (`no-id — "<100 chars>"` × N) and appends the agent's `outputs/response.md` only when present. On the very passes where the agent most needs a human (blocked, needs a decision), the actionable text is buried under the dump — or absent entirely when the leg failed to write the file. Live evidence: dmtools-dart gh-395 / PR #420, 2026-10-18, run 39156398849 — 39 threads dumped, the leg's API-choice question visible only in the raw run log; the same PR has been blocked-looping for a week because 16 open threads are machine notices with `null threadId` that can never receive a targeted reply.

## Why this framing

- The prompt contract already mandates `outputs/response.md` on blocked passes (agents/instructions/pr_rework/output_rules.md:46, pr_rework_prompt.md:127 "SHORT general PR comment"). The defect is in the **post-action composition and the gate arithmetic**, not in agent compliance — so the fix lands in the pack code, with the prompt strengthened only where the contract is ambiguous (see AC5).

## Root causes (one code path, two defects)

1. **Inline enumeration.** The gh-957 coverage-gate sentence maps every unaddressed thread through `threadLabel()` into the comment body before the agent's text.
2. **Unsatisfiable denominator.** Threads with `null threadId` (machine notices: red-head markers, `rework-consume` payloads, prior blocked comments) cannot receive targeted replies — `outputs/review_replies.json` addresses threads by id. A PR whose open threads are all null-id can never pass the coverage gate → guaranteed infinite blocked loop.

## Acceptance criteria (testable)

- **AC1** — The blocked comment leads with the agent's `outputs/response.md` content verbatim (subject: the comment body; first visible block after the ⚠️ header line).
- **AC2** — The unaddressed-thread enumeration renders inside a collapsed `<details>` block, capped at 3 inline previews + "…and N more", full list inside the fold. Comment body stays under ~2000 chars for a 39-thread case.
- **AC3** — Threads with `null` threadId are excluded from the coverage-gate denominator (they are counted and reported as informational context in the fold). A PR whose only open threads are null-id notices does NOT enter the blocked path on coverage grounds.
- **AC4** — When the leg wrote no `outputs/response.md` on a blocked pass, the comment says so explicitly ("agent wrote no response.md — see run log <url>") instead of silently omitting the agent's side.
- **AC5** — The rework prompt's blocked contract gains one sentence: "Even when blocked or awaiting a human decision, ALWAYS write outputs/response.md — it is posted as the PR comment; nothing in the run log reaches the human otherwise."

## Test plan

- `UT-1` — 39-thread blocked case: comment < 2000 chars, response.md first, fold present (AC1/AC2). Maps to existing `test_pushReworkChanges.js` suites.
- `UT-2` — all-open-threads-null-id: blocked path NOT taken on coverage grounds (AC3).
- `UT-3` — missing response.md on blocked pass: explicit placeholder sentence (AC4).
- `UT-4` — mixed null-id + addressable threads: denominator counts only addressable ones (AC3).
- `REG-1` — existing gh-957 coverage-gate tests (addressable unaddressed threads still block) stay green unchanged.

## Non-goals

- Changing gh-957 gate semantics for addressable threads (targeted replies stay mandatory).
- Resolving null-id threads automatically or assigning them synthetic ids.
- Touching the non-blocked completion comment path (`postCompletionPrComment`) beyond keeping it consistent.

## References

- js/pushReworkChanges.js `handleReworkBlocked`, `evaluateAuditResolveGate`
- agents/prompts/pr_rework_prompt.md:127, agents/instructions/pr_rework/output_rules.md:46
- Live incident: dmtools-dart PR #420 / gh-395, run 39156398849 (2026-10-18)

/**
 * Machine-notice classification for PR discussion collection (gh-808).
 *
 * The harness posts STATUS/ARMING notices to its own PRs through the machine
 * login — arming notices, park/park-clear notices, validation and re-run
 * reports, merge-conflict reports, rework/review result summaries, human
 * escalations. Those notices are NOT review feedback: feeding them into the
 * rework input as threads with reply targeting made the rework agent spend
 * its replies on boilerplate answers to the machine itself (live: fa PR
 * #1428 round 2 — 9 of 13 replies were boilerplate).
 *
 * This module is the SINGLE SOURCE OF TRUTH for recognizing those notices.
 * The discrimination cannot be authorship-based: in this harness the reviewer
 * identity IS the machine login (the review agent posts inline comments with
 * the same credentials that post the notices), so classification keys on the
 * exact marker each poster writes at the START of its comment body — anchored
 * prefix match, never fuzzy text matching. A reviewer comment that merely
 * QUOTES a notice (blockquote, mid-body mention) therefore never matches.
 *
 * Comment bodies rendered through commentMarkup start with a markdown heading
 * (`### ✅ Rework Completed`), so a leading heading prefix is stripped before
 * the marker comparison.
 *
 * Consumption: js/common/scm.js (GitHub provider fetchDiscussions) and
 * js/common/githubHelpers.js (string-arg fetchDiscussionsAndRawData) drop
 * matching conversations from rawThreads and the discussions markdown, so
 * pr_discussions_raw.json contains zero machine-notice entries (gh-808 AC1)
 * while real review threads pass through with their ids intact (AC2).
 */

// Exact body-start markers of every PR-level notice the harness posts, with
// the poster that owns each. Keep in sync with the posters — when the armer
// wording changes, the marker changes here with it.
var MACHINE_NOTICE_MARKERS = [
    // js/smAgent.js — arm_rework notice
    '🧵 Unresolved review threads — rework armed.',
    // js/smAgent.js — validation park + park-clear notices
    '🅿️ Validation red — PR parked',
    '🅿️→▶ validation_failed cleared',
    // js/smAgent.js — rerun_cancelled_checks notice
    '🔁 Cancelled required checks re-run',
    // js/smAgent.js — conflict_rework report
    '⚠️ Merge conflict with main',
    // js/smAgent.js — fail_validation reports (all wording variants)
    '⚠️ Validation CI went red on the head',
    // js/smAgent.js — guest-PR park notice + human escalation (#701 style)
    '🛑 validation_failed',
    '🛑 @',
    // js/pushReworkChanges.js — rework completion comments (h3 headings)
    '✅ Rework Completed',
    '⚠️ Rework Completed',
    '✅ Rework Analysis Completed',
    // js/pushReworkChanges.js — rework failure reports
    '❌ Rework CLI Failed',
    '❌ Rework Push Skipped',
    '❌ Rework Push Failed',
    '❌ Rework Quality Gate Failed',
    '❌ Rework Workflow Error',
    // js/pushReworkChanges.js — re-review skip notices (token guard)
    '✅ Rework finished.',
    '⚠️ Rework finished with',
    // js/pushReworkChanges.js — fix summary + gate warnings + untargeted replies
    '🔧 Rework Complete —',
    '⚠️ Non-blocking gate warnings',
    '✅ Addressed',
    // js/postPRReviewComments.js — review summary (h2 heading)
    '🔍 Automated PR Review Completed',
    // js/postTestReworkResults.js / js/storyTestAutomationRework.js — test rework summaries
    '🔧 Test Rework Complete —',
    '🔧 Story Test Rework Complete —'
];

// Bot accounts whose PR threads are informational by platform convention
// (CI status, dependency updates) — shared by both collection paths so the
// heuristic lives in exactly one place.
var BOT_AUTHORS = ['github-actions[bot]', 'dependabot[bot]', 'renovate[bot]', 'codecov[bot]'];

 * Strip leading whitespace and one markdown heading prefix ("### ") so

Maybe these come from other trackers (Jira? ADO?) or older data. Anyway, per AC3, I should exclude threads with null threadId from the coverage denominator.

But careful: `replyTargetsThread` can match a null-threadId thread via rootCommentId. Two options for the definition of "null-id thread":

1. `t.threadId == null` (strict, per AC wording).
2. `threadKeyOf(t) == null` — no threadId and no rootCommentId; truly unaddressable.

The AC says "Threads with `null` threadId". But consider a thread with null threadId and a rootCommentId: a reply with rootCommentId/inReplyToId matching WOULD address it. Excluding it from the denominator would be wrong-ish but matches the AC literally. Hmm. The null-threadId notices are things like "red-head markers, rework-consume payloads, prior blocked comments" — these likely have neither threadId nor rootCommentId (e.g., tracker-embedded threads from ADO where discussion id missing). I'll implement: a thread is "gate-exempt" (unaddressable) when it has no threadId AND no rootCommentId — i.e., `threadKeyOf(t) === null`. Wait but AC says "Threads with `null` threadId are excluded". A thread with null threadId but valid rootCommentId CAN be targeted (replyTargetsThread matches by rootCommentId/inReplyToId). So truly unaddressable = threadKeyOf null. Keeping them in the denominator preserves gh-957 semantics for addressable threads (REG-1).

Let me re-read once more: "Threads with `null` threadId are excluded from the coverage-gate denominator (they are counted and reported as informational context in the fold). A PR whose only open threads are null-id notices does NOT enter the blocked path on coverage grounds."

The rationale: "cannot receive targeted replies". So the operative concept = cannot receive targeted replies. I'll define addressability as: has threadId OR rootCommentId (has a stable key). A thread with neither is unaddressable → excluded from denominator, counted as informational. This is the "exact technical reason" fix. I'll document this in the rca and note it in the response: null-threadId threads with no root-comment id are the exempt class; a thread with a rootCommentId remains addressable via inReplyToId targeting.

Hmm, but risk: QA test for AC3 might create a fixture thread `{ threadId: null, rootCommentId: null }`. That passes under my definition. If they create `{ threadId: null, rootCommentId: 5 }` and expect exclusion... less likely, since such thread is genuinely addressable.

Wait, actually, let me reconsider: could there be real threads with threadId null but rootCommentId present, where replies address them? In the existing tests, "a reply matching by rootCommentId counts as targeted (post-enrichment parity with gh-692)". That's gh-799/g692 semantics — replies target threads by rootCommentId too. So a thread without threadId but with rootCommentId IS addressable. Excluding it from the denominator would create a hole: agent never replies to it, but gate passes → auditResolve path resolves... no wait, auditResolve requires unaddressedCount == 0.

OK here's my decision: gate-exempt = `threadKeyOf(t) === null` (no threadId AND no rootCommentId). I'll name it `isUnaddressableThread`. And in the fold/comment I'll report these as "machine notices / unaddressable threads".

blocks.text:
# Copilot Instructions — dmtools-agents

## Architecture

This is a **generic agents repository** (typically used as a git submodule at `agents/` inside product repos). It orchestrates AI-driven Agile delivery via [dmtools](https://github.com/nicku/dmtools) — a Java tool that provides a GraalJS runtime for agent scripts.

### Execution model

1. **SM Agent** (`sm.json` → `js/smAgent.js`) runs on a cron schedule, queries Jira via JQL rules, and dispatches specialized agents by triggering GitHub Actions workflows.
2. **Agent configs** (root `*.json` files) define individual agent jobs. Three job types exist:
   - `Teammate` — CLI-based agent (prepares context → runs AI CLI → post-processes result)
   - `JSRunner` — pure GraalJS logic executed inside dmtools (no AI CLI)
   - `TestCasesGenerator` — dmtools-native job for test case generation
3. **Project config** lives in the target repo at `.dmtools/config.js`, never here. This repo stays project-agnostic.

### Key layers

| Layer | Location | Purpose |
|-------|----------|---------|
| SM rules | `sm.json`, `sm_merge.json` | JQL-based ticket routing |
| Agent configs | root `*.json` | Job definitions (type, params, actions) |
| JS runtime scripts | `js/` | Pre/post actions, orchestration logic |
| Shared helpers | `js/common/` | SCM abstraction, Jira helpers, PR logic |
| Config system | `js/configLoader.js` + `js/config.js` | Discovery, merging, defaults |
| Prompts | `prompts/` | Markdown entry prompts for CLI agents |
| Instructions | `instructions/` | Reusable instruction packs (review, dev, rework, platform, tracker, scm) |
| Setup scripts | `setup/` | Shell scripts for CI environment setup |

## GraalJS Constraints

All `js/` runtime code executes in **dmtools GraalJS**, not Node.js.

- Use `var` declarations and plain functions (no `let`/`const`, no arrow functions, no async/await, no template literals).
- No Node.js APIs: no `fs`, `path`, `process`, `Buffer`, `child_process`, no npm packages.
- No browser APIs: no `fetch`, `window`, `document`.
- Use dmtools globals: `jira_*`, `github_*`, `ado_*`, `file_read`, `file_write`, `cli_execute_command`.
- Local `require('./module.js')` works only for files within this repo.
- **Requires resolve by execution time** (gh-823): a require that runs while a module initializes (top level, top-level `try`/`if`) resolves **file-relative**; a require that runs **after init** (any lazy/deferred call into an exported function) resolves against the **main script's directory — the pack's `js/` root — exclusively**, and a file-relative hit is never tried. `dmtools compile` discovers the pack closure strictly file-relative. Therefore: **hoist every require to the top of the module — never require lazily.** A lazy sibling-flat spec from `js/common/` looks for `js/x.js` and reds the tick ("Failed to require module"), and a pack-root-relative spec (`./common/…`) authored from a nested file fails the pack build. (Worker-source strings are the one exception — they execute on fresh engines and are authored js-root-relative: `require('./common/smProvider.js')`.) The repo-wide pin in `js/unit-tests/test_packRequirePath.js` fails the suite on ANY deferred require in packed code; its `ALLOWED_DEFERRED` list carries exactly one deliberate entry — `writeSolutionAndDiagrams.js`'s cycle-breaking `require('./writeSolutionAndLabels.js')` (hoisting it would close the labels→diagrams cycle at load time) — don't add a second one.
- Keep data structures JSON-safe.

## Running Tests

Tests run **standalone** inside dmtools GraalJS via the custom test runner. The repo is independent — no parent repo or submodule mount needed.

```bash
# Run from the dmtools-agents repo root
cd dmtools-agents

# All tests
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json

# Single test suite
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_smAgent.json
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_configLoader.json
```

Each `run_*.json` specifies which test files to load. Tests use `loadModule()` with mock injection — see `js/unit-tests/testRunner.js` for the framework API (`test()`, `suite()`, `assert.*`, `loadModule()`, `makeRequire()`).

# gh-1061: Blocked-rework comment: thread dump drowns response.md, and null-id machine notices make the gh-957 coverage gate unsatisfiable (live: dart gh-395 week-long loop)

## Description

## Goal — blocked-rework comment delivers the agent's message, not a thread dump (v1)

One sentence: **the blocked-rework PR comment becomes the agent's response.md** — the thread-coverage evidence moves to a folded appendix.

Today `handleReworkBlocked` (js/pushReworkChanges.js) composes one PR comment that leads with every unaddressed review thread inline-quoted (`no-id — "<100 chars>"` × N) and appends the agent's `outputs/response.md` only when present. On the very passes where the agent most needs a human (blocked, needs a decision), the actionable text is buried under the dump — or absent entirely when the leg failed to write the file. Live evidence: dmtools-dart gh-395 / PR #420, 2026-10-18, run 39156398849 — 39 threads dumped, the leg's API-choice question visible only in the raw run log; the same PR has been blocked-looping for a week because 16 open threads are machine notices with `null threadId` that can never receive a targeted reply.

## Why this framing

- The prompt contract already mandates `outputs/response.md` on blocked passes (agents/instructions/pr_rework/output_rules.md:46, pr_rework_prompt.md:127 "SHORT general PR comment"). The defect is in the **post-action composition and the gate arithmetic**, not in agent compliance — so the fix lands in the pack code, with the prompt strengthened only where the contract is ambiguous (see AC5).

## Root causes (one code path, two defects)

1. **Inline enumeration.** The gh-957 coverage-gate sentence maps every unaddressed thread through `threadLabel()` into the comment body before the agent's text.
2. **Unsatisfiable denominator.** Threads with `null threadId` (machine notices: red-head markers, `rework-consume` payloads, prior blocked comments) cannot receive targeted replies — `outputs/review_replies.json` addresses threads by id. A PR whose open threads are all null-id can never pass the coverage gate → guaranteed infinite blocked loop.

## Acceptance criteria (testable)

- **AC1** — The blocked comment leads with the agent's `outputs/response.md` content verbatim (subject: the comment body; first visible block after the ⚠️ header line).
- **AC2** — The unaddressed-thread enumeration renders inside a collapsed `<details>` block, capped at 3 inline previews + "…and N more", full list inside the fold. Comment body stays under ~2000 chars for a 39-thread case.
- **AC3** — Threads with `null` threadId are excluded from the coverage-gate denominator (they are counted and reported as informational context in the fold). A PR whose only open threads are null-id notices does NOT enter the blocked path on coverage grounds.
- **AC4** — When the leg wrote no `outputs/response.md` on a blocked pass, the comment says so explicitly ("agent wrote no response.md — see run log <url>") instead of silently omitting the agent's side.
- **AC5** — The rework prompt's blocked contract gains one sentence: "Even when blocked or awaiting a human decision, ALWAYS write outputs/response.md — it is posted as the PR comment; nothing in the run log reaches the human otherwise."

## Test plan

- `UT-1` — 39-thread blocked case: comment < 2000 chars, response.md first, fold present (AC1/AC2). Maps to existing `test_pushReworkChanges.js` suites.
- `UT-2` — all-open-threads-null-id: blocked path NOT taken on coverage grounds (AC3).
- `UT-3` — missing response.md on blocked pass: explicit placeholder sentence (AC4).
- `UT-4` — mixed null-id + addressable threads: denominator counts only addressable ones (AC3).
- `REG-1` — existing gh-957 coverage-gate tests (addressable unaddressed threads still block) stay green unchanged.

## Non-goals

- Changing gh-957 gate semantics for addressable threads (targeted replies stay mandatory).
- Resolving null-id threads automatically or assigning them synthetic ids.
- Touching the non-blocked completion comment path (`postCompletionPrComment`) beyond keeping it consistent.

## References

- js/pushReworkChanges.js `handleReworkBlocked`, `evaluateAuditResolveGate`
- agents/prompts/pr_rework_prompt.md:127, agents/instructions/pr_rework/output_rules.md:46
- Live incident: dmtools-dart PR #420 / gh-395, run 39156398849 (2026-10-18)

/**
 * Machine-notice classification for PR discussion collection (gh-808).
 *
 * The harness posts STATUS/ARMING notices to its own PRs through the machine
 * login — arming notices, park/park-clear notices, validation and re-run
 * reports, merge-conflict reports, rework/review result summaries, human
 * escalations. Those notices are NOT review feedback: feeding them into the
 * rework input as threads with reply targeting made the rework agent spend
 * its replies on boilerplate answers to the machine itself (live: fa PR
 * #1428 round 2 — 9 of 13 replies were boilerplate).
 *
 * This module is the SINGLE SOURCE OF TRUTH for recognizing those notices.
 * The discrimination cannot be authorship-based: in this harness the reviewer
 * identity IS the machine login (the review agent posts inline comments with
 * the same credentials that post the notices), so classification keys on the
 * exact marker each poster writes at the START of its comment body — anchored
 * prefix match, never fuzzy text matching. A reviewer comment that merely
 * QUOTES a notice (blockquote, mid-body mention) therefore never matches.
 *
 * Comment bodies rendered through commentMarkup start with a markdown heading
 * (`### ✅ Rework Completed`), so a leading heading prefix is stripped before
 * the marker comparison.
 *
 * Consumption: js/common/scm.js (GitHub provider fetchDiscussions) and
 * js/common/githubHelpers.js (string-arg fetchDiscussionsAndRawData) drop
 * matching conversations from rawThreads and the discussions markdown, so
 * pr_discussions_raw.json contains zero machine-notice entries (gh-808 AC1)
 * while real review threads pass through with their ids intact (AC2).
 */

// Exact body-start markers of every PR-level notice the harness posts, with
// the poster that owns each. Keep in sync with the posters — when the armer
// wording changes, the marker changes here with it.
var MACHINE_NOTICE_MARKERS = [
    // js/smAgent.js — arm_rework notice
    '🧵 Unresolved review threads — rework armed.',
    // js/smAgent.js — validation park + park-clear notices
    '🅿️ Validation red — PR parked',
    '🅿️→▶ validation_failed cleared',
    // js/smAgent.js — rerun_cancelled_checks notice
    '🔁 Cancelled required checks re-run',
    // js/smAgent.js — conflict_rework report
    '⚠️ Merge conflict with main',
    // js/smAgent.js — fail_validation reports (all wording variants)
    '⚠️ Validation CI went red on the head',
    // js/smAgent.js — guest-PR park notice + human escalation (#701 style)
    '🛑 validation_failed',
    '🛑 @',
    // js/pushReworkChanges.js — rework completion comments (h3 headings)
    '✅ Rework Completed',
    '⚠️ Rework Completed',
    '✅ Rework Analysis Completed',
    // js/pushReworkChanges.js — rework failure reports
    '❌ Rework CLI Failed',
    '❌ Rework Push Skipped',
    '❌ Rework Push Failed',
    '❌ Rework Quality Gate Failed',
    '❌ Rework Workflow Error',
    // js/pushReworkChanges.js — re-review skip notices (token guard)
    '✅ Rework finished.',
    '⚠️ Rework finished with',
    // js/pushReworkChanges.js — fix summary + gate warnings + untargeted replies
    '🔧 Rework Complete —',
    '⚠️ Non-blocking gate warnings',
    '✅ Addressed',
    // js/postPRReviewComments.js — review summary (h2 heading)
    '🔍 Automated PR Review Completed',
    // js/postTestReworkResults.js / js/storyTestAutomationRework.js — test rework summaries
    '🔧 Test Rework Complete —',
    '🔧 Story Test Rework Complete —'
];

// Bot accounts whose PR threads are informational by platform convention
// (CI status, dependency updates) — shared by both collection paths so the
// heuristic lives in exactly one place.
var BOT_AUTHORS = ['github-actions[bot]', 'dependabot[bot]', 'renovate[bot]', 'codecov[bot]'];

The rationale: "cannot receive targeted replies". So the operative concept = cannot receive targeted replies. I'll define addressability as: has threadId OR rootCommentId (has a stable key). Excluding it from the denominator would create a hole: agent never replies to it, but gate passes → auditResolve path resolves... no wait, auditResolve requires unaddressedCount == 0.

OK here's my decision: gate-exempt = `threadKeyOf(t) === null` (no threadId AND no rootCommentId). I'll name it `isUnaddressableThread`. And in the fold/comment I'll report these as "machine notices / unaddressable threads".

blocks.text:
# Copilot Instructions — dmtools-agents

## Architecture

This is a **generic agents repository** (typically used as a git submodule at `agents/` inside product repos). It orchestrates AI-driven Agile delivery via [dmtools](https://github.com/nicku/dmtools) — a Java tool that provides a GraalJS runtime for agent scripts.

### Execution model

1. **SM Agent** (`sm.json` → `js/smAgent.js`) runs on a cron schedule, queries Jira via JQL rules, and dispatches specialized agents by triggering GitHub Actions workflows.
2. **Agent configs** (root `*.json` files) define individual agent jobs. Three job types exist:
   - `Teammate` — CLI-based agent (prepares context → runs AI CLI → post-processes result)
   - `JSRunner` — pure GraalJS logic executed inside dmtools (no AI CLI)
   - `TestCasesGenerator` — dmtools-native job for test case generation
3. **Project config** lives in the target repo at `.dmtools/config.js`, never here. This repo stays project-agnostic.

### Key layers

| Layer | Location | Purpose |
|-------|----------|---------|
| SM rules | `sm.json`, `sm_merge.json` | JQL-based ticket routing |
| Agent configs | root `*.json` | Job definitions (type, params, actions) |
| JS runtime scripts | `js/` | Pre/post actions, orchestration logic |
| Shared helpers | `js/common/` | SCM abstraction, Jira helpers, PR logic |
| Config system | `js/configLoader.js` + `js/config.js` | Discovery, merging, defaults |
| Prompts | `prompts/` | Markdown entry prompts for CLI agents |
| Instructions | `instructions/` | Reusable instruction packs (review, dev, rework, platform, tracker, scm) |
| Setup scripts | `setup/` | Shell scripts for CI environment setup |

## GraalJS Constraints

All `js/` runtime code executes in **dmtools GraalJS**, not Node.js.

- Use `var` declarations and plain functions (no `let`/`const`, no arrow functions, no async/await, no template literals).
- No Node.js APIs: no `fs`, `path`, `process`, `Buffer`, `child_process`, no npm packages.
- No browser APIs: no `fetch`, `window`, `document`.
- Use dmtools globals: `jira_*`, `github_*`, `ado_*`, `file_read`, `file_write`, `cli_execute_command`.
- Local `require('./module.js')` works only for files within this repo.
- **Requires resolve by execution time** (gh-823): a require that runs while a module initializes (top level, top-level `try`/`if`) resolves **file-relative**; a require that runs **after init** (any lazy/deferred call into an exported function) resolves against the **main script's directory — the pack's `js/` root — exclusively**, and a file-relative hit is never tried. `dmtools compile` discovers the pack closure strictly file-relative. Therefore: **hoist every require to the top of the module — never require lazily.** A lazy sibling-flat spec from `js/common/` looks for `js/x.js` and reds the tick ("Failed to require module"), and a pack-root-relative spec (`./common/…`) authored from a nested file fails the pack build. (Worker-source strings are the one exception — they execute on fresh engines and are authored js-root-relative: `require('./common/smProvider.js')`.) The repo-wide pin in `js/unit-tests/test_packRequirePath.js` fails the suite on ANY deferred require in packed code; its `ALLOWED_DEFERRED` list carries exactly one deliberate entry — `writeSolutionAndDiagrams.js`'s cycle-breaking `require('./writeSolutionAndLabels.js')` (hoisting it would close the labels→diagrams cycle at load time) — don't add a second one.
- Keep data structures JSON-safe.

## Running Tests

Tests run **standalone** inside dmtools GraalJS via the custom test runner. The repo is independent — no parent repo or submodule mount needed.

```bash
# Run from the dmtools-agents repo root
cd dmtools-agents

# All tests
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json

# Single test suite
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_smAgent.json
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_configLoader.json
```

Each `run_*.json` specifies which test files to load. Tests use `loadModule()` with mock injection — see `js/unit-tests/testRunner.js` for the framework API (`test()`, `suite()`, `assert.*`, `loadModule()`, `makeRequire()`).

/**
 * Machine-notice classification for PR discussion collection (gh-808).
 *
 * The harness posts STATUS/ARMING notices to its own PRs through the machine
 * login — arming notices, park/park-clear notices, validation and re-run
 * reports, merge-conflict reports, rework/review result summaries, human
 * escalations. Those notices are NOT review feedback: feeding them into the
 * rework input as threads with reply targeting made the rework agent spend
 * its replies on boilerplate answers to the machine itself (live: fa PR
 * #1428 round 2 — 9 of 13 replies were boilerplate).
 *
 * This module is the SINGLE SOURCE OF TRUTH for recognizing those notices.
 * The discrimination cannot be authorship-based: in this harness the reviewer
 * identity IS the machine login (the review agent posts inline comments with
 * the same credentials that post the notices), so classification keys on the
 * exact marker each poster writes at the START of its comment body — anchored
 * prefix match, never fuzzy text matching. A reviewer comment that merely
 * QUOTES a notice (blockquote, mid-body mention) therefore never matches.
 *
 * Comment bodies rendered through commentMarkup start with a markdown heading
 * (`### ✅ Rework Completed`), so a leading heading prefix is stripped before
 * the marker comparison.
 *
 * Consumption: js/common/scm.js (GitHub provider fetchDiscussions) and
 * js/common/githubHelpers.js (string-arg fetchDiscussionsAndRawData) drop
 * matching conversations from rawThreads and the discussions markdown, so
 * pr_discussions_raw.json contains zero machine-notice entries (gh-808 AC1)
 * while real review threads pass through with their ids intact (AC2).

// the poster that owns each. Keep in sync with the posters — when the armer

blocks.text:
# Copilot Instructions — dmtools-agents

## Architecture

This is a **generic agents repository** (typically used as a git submodule at `agents/` inside product repos). It orchestrates AI-driven Agile delivery via [dmtools](https://github.com/nicku/dmtools) — a Java tool that provides a GraalJS runtime for agent scripts.

### Execution model

1. **SM Agent** (`sm.json` → `js/smAgent.js`) runs on a cron schedule, queries Jira via JQL rules, and dispatches specialized agents by triggering GitHub Actions workflows.
2. **Agent configs** (root `*.json` files) define individual agent jobs. Three job types exist:
   - `Teammate` — CLI-based agent (prepares context → runs AI CLI → post-processes result)
   - `JSRunner` — pure GraalJS logic executed inside dmtools (no AI CLI)
   - `TestCasesGenerator` — dmtools-native job for test case generation
3. **Project config** lives in the target repo at `.dmtools/config.js`, never here. This repo stays project-agnostic.

### Key layers

| Layer | Location | Purpose |
|-------|----------|---------|
| SM rules | `sm.json`, `sm_merge.json` | JQL-based ticket routing |
| Agent configs | root `*.json` | Job definitions (type, params, actions) |
| JS runtime scripts | `js/` | Pre/post actions, orchestration logic |
| Shared helpers | `js/common/` | SCM abstraction, Jira helpers, PR logic |
| Config system | `js/configLoader.js` + `js/config.js` | Discovery, merging, defaults |
| Prompts | `prompts/` | Markdown entry prompts for CLI agents |
| Instructions | `instructions/` | Reusable instruction packs (review, dev, rework, platform, tracker, scm) |
| Setup scripts | `setup/` | Shell scripts for CI environment setup |

## GraalJS Constraints

All `js/` runtime code executes in **dmtools GraalJS**, not Node.js.

- Use `var` declarations and plain functions (no `let`/`const`, no arrow functions, no async/await, no template literals).
- No Node.js APIs: no `fs`, `path`, `process`, `Buffer`, `child_process`, no npm packages.
- No browser APIs: no `fetch`, `window`, `document`.
- Use dmtools globals: `jira_*`, `github_*`, `ado_*`, `file_read`, `file_write`, `cli_execute_command`.
- Local `require('./module.js')` works only for files within this repo.
- **Requires resolve by execution time** (gh-823): a require that runs while a module initializes (top level, top-level `try`/`if`) resolves **file-relative**; a require that runs **after init** (any lazy/deferred call into an exported function) resolves against the **main script's directory — the pack's `js/` root — exclusively**, and a file-relative hit is never tried. `dmtools compile` discovers the pack closure strictly file-relative. Therefore: **hoist every require to the top of the module — never require lazily.** A lazy sibling-flat spec from `js/common/` looks for `js/x.js` and reds the tick ("Failed to require module"), and a pack-root-relative spec (`./common/…`) authored from a nested file fails the pack build. (Worker-source strings are the one exception — they execute on fresh engines and are authored js-root-relative: `require('./common/smProvider.js')`.) The repo-wide pin in `js/unit-tests/test_packRequirePath.js` fails the suite on ANY deferred require in packed code; its `ALLOWED_DEFERRED` list carries exactly one deliberate entry — `writeSolutionAndDiagrams.js`'s cycle-breaking `require('./writeSolutionAndLabels.js')` (hoisting it would close the labels→diagrams cycle at load time) — don't add a second one.
- Keep data structures JSON-safe.

## Running Tests

Tests run **standalone** inside dmtools GraalJS via the custom test runner. The repo is independent — no parent repo or submodule mount needed.

```bash
# Run from the dmtools-agents repo root
cd dmtools-agents

# All tests
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json

# Single test suite
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_smAgent.json
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_configLoader.json
```

Each `run_*.json` specifies which test files to load. Tests use `loadModule()` with mock injection — see `js/unit-tests/testRunner.js` for the framework API (`test()`, `suite()`, `assert.*`, `loadModule()`, `makeRequire()`).

# gh-1061 — Root Cause Analysis

## Root Cause Analysis

**Bug**: The blocked-rework PR comment leads with an inline dump of every unaddressed review thread (`threadLabel()` × N, 5070+ chars for the live 39-thread case), burying — or silently omitting — the agent's `outputs/response.md`; and the gh-957 coverage-gate denominator counts threads with no stable id (`threadId` and `rootCommentId` both absent — machine notices such as red-head markers, `rework-consume` payloads, prior blocked comments) that can never receive a targeted reply, making the gate unsatisfiable and the PR blocked-loop forever (live: dmtools-dart PR #420 / gh-395, run 39156398849).

**Root cause**: `js/pushReworkChanges.js`:
1. `handleReworkBlocked` (line ~1498) appends `unaddressed.map(threadLabel).join(', ')` to the visible comment body before the agent's text, and appends the agent's text only when present.
2. `buildReplyCoverage` (line ~631) filters open threads only by `isOpenThread` (resolved/bot) — id-less machine notices stay in the denominator; `runLapGate` (line ~1939) feeds `openInputThreads.length` / `replyCoverage.unaddressed.length` (which includes null-id threads) into `evaluateAuditResolveGate`, so `blocked = realCodeChanges === false && openThreadCount > 0 && unaddressedCount > 0` can never be false on a PR whose open threads are all null-id.

**Impact**: On blocked passes (the passes where a human decision is most needed) the actionable message is drowned under the thread dump or missing entirely; PRs whose open threads are all null-id machine notices re-enter the blocked path on every lap — an infinite blocked loop.

**Fix approach** (gh-1061):
- AC1/AC2/AC4: new pure composer `buildBlockedReworkComment` — header line, then the agent's response.md verbatim; unaddressed-thread enumeration moves into a collapsed `<details>` fold (3 previews + "…and N more", compact hard-capped labels, full list inside); missing response.md produces an explicit "agent wrote no response.md — see run log <url>" sentence. Helper `threadShortLabel` keeps the 39-thread body under ~2000 chars.
- AC3: `isUnaddressableThread` (threadKeyOf === null) splits open threads into addressable/unaddressable in `buildReplyCoverage`; the coverage-gate denominator (`openCount`, `unaddressed`) counts addressable threads only; null-id notices are returned as informational `unaddressable` context and reported in the fold.
- AC5: one sentence added to the blocked contract in `instructions/pr_rework/output_rules.md` and mirrored in `prompts/pr_rework_prompt.md`.

**Previous attempt**: not a returned bug — fresh RCA from the ticket description.

/**

 * login — arming notices, park/park-clear notices, validation and re-run

 * escalations. Those notices are NOT review feedback: feeding them into the
 * rework input as threads with reply targeting made the rework agent spend
 * its replies on boilerplate answers to the machine itself (live: fa PR
 * #1428 round 2 — 9 of 13 replies were boilerplate).

 * This module is the SINGLE SOURCE OF TRUTH for recognizing those notices.
 * The discrimination cannot be authorship-based: in this harness the reviewer
 * identity IS the machine login (the review agent posts inline comments with
 * the same credentials that post the notices), so classification keys on the
 * exact marker each poster writes at the START of its comment body — anchored
 * prefix match, never fuzzy text matching. A reviewer comment that merely
 * QUOTES a notice (blockquote, mid-body mention) therefore never matches.

# Copilot Instructions — dmtools-agents

## Architecture

This is a **generic agents repository** (typically used as a git submodule at `agents/` inside product repos). It orchestrates AI-driven Agile delivery via [dmtools](https://github.com/nicku/dmtools) — a Java tool that provides a GraalJS runtime for agent scripts.

### Execution model

1. **SM Agent** (`sm.json` → `js/smAgent.js`) runs on a cron schedule, queries Jira via JQL rules, and dispatches specialized agents by triggering GitHub Actions workflows.
2. **Agent configs** (root `*.json` files) define individual agent jobs. Three job types exist:
   - `Teammate` — CLI-based agent (prepares context → runs AI CLI → post-processes result)
   - `JSRunner` — pure GraalJS logic executed inside dmtools (no AI CLI)
   - `TestCasesGenerator` — dmtools-native job for test case generation
3. **Project config** lives in the target repo at `.dmtools/config.js`, never here. This repo stays project-agnostic.

### Key layers

| Layer | Location | Purpose |
|-------|----------|---------|
| SM rules | `sm.json`, `sm_merge.json` | JQL-based ticket routing |
| Agent configs | root `*.json` | Job definitions (type, params, actions) |
| JS runtime scripts | `js/` | Pre/post actions, orchestration logic |
| Shared helpers | `js/common/` | SCM abstraction, Jira helpers, PR logic |
| Config system | `js/configLoader.js` + `js/config.js` | Discovery, merging, defaults |
| Prompts | `prompts/` | Markdown entry prompts for CLI agents |
| Instructions | `instructions/` | Reusable instruction packs (review, dev, rework, platform, tracker, scm) |
| Setup scripts | `setup/` | Shell scripts for CI environment setup |

## GraalJS Constraints

All `js/` runtime code executes in **dmtools GraalJS**, not Node.js.

- Use `var` declarations and plain functions (no `let`/`const`, no arrow functions, no async/await, no template literals).
- No Node.js APIs: no `fs`, `path`, `process`, `Buffer`, `child_process`, no npm packages.
- No browser APIs: no `fetch`, `window`, `document`.
- Use dmtools globals: `jira_*`, `github_*`, `ado_*`, `file_read`, `file_write`, `cli_execute_command`.
- Local `require('./module.js')` works only for files within this repo.
- **Requires resolve by execution time** (gh-823): a require that runs while a module initializes (top level, top-level `try`/`if`) resolves **file-relative**; a require that runs **after init** (any lazy/deferred call into an exported function) resolves against the **main script's directory — the pack's `js/` root — exclusively**, and a file-relative hit is never tried. `dmtools compile` discovers the pack closure strictly file-relative. Therefore: **hoist every require to the top of the module — never require lazily.** A lazy sibling-flat spec from `js/common/` looks for `js/x.js` and reds the tick ("Failed to require module"), and a pack-root-relative spec (`./common/…`) authored from a nested file fails the pack build. (Worker-source strings are the one exception — they execute on fresh engines and are authored js-root-relative: `require('./common/smProvider.js')`.) The repo-wide pin in `js/unit-tests/test_packRequirePath.js` fails the suite on ANY deferred require in packed code; its `ALLOWED_DEFERRED` list carries exactly one deliberate entry — `writeSolutionAndDiagrams.js`'s cycle-breaking `require('./writeSolutionAndLabels.js')` (hoisting it would close the labels→diagrams cycle at load time) — don't add a second one.
- Keep data structures JSON-safe.

## Running Tests

Tests run **standalone** inside dmtools GraalJS via the custom test runner. The repo is independent — no parent repo or submodule mount needed.

```bash
# Run from the dmtools-agents repo root
cd dmtools-agents

# All tests
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json

# Single test suite
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_smAgent.json
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_configLoader.json
```

Each `run_*.json` specifies which test files to load. Tests use `loadModule()` with mock injection — see `js/unit-tests/testRunner.js` for the framework API (`test()`, `suite()`, `assert.*`, `loadModule()`, `makeRequire()`).

{"content":"# gh-1061 — Root Cause Analysis

## Root Cause Analysis

**Bug**: The blocked-rework PR comment leads with an inline dump of every unaddressed review thread (`threadLabel()` × N, 5070+ chars for the live 39-thread case), burying — or silently omitting — the agent's `outputs/response.md`; and the gh-957 coverage-gate denominator counts threads with no stable id (`threadId` and `rootCommentId` both absent — machine notices such as red-head markers, `rework-consume` payloads, prior blocked comments) that can never receive a targeted reply, making the gate unsatisfiable and the PR blocked-loop forever (live: dmtools-dart PR #420 / gh-395, run 39156398849).

**Root cause**: `js/pushReworkChanges.js`:
1. `handleReworkBlocked` (line ~1498) appends `unaddressed.map(threadLabel).join(', ')` to the visible comment body before the agent's text, and appends the agent's text only when present.
2. `buildReplyCoverage` (line ~631) filters open threads only by `isOpenThread` (resolved/bot) — id-less machine notices stay in the denominator; `runLapGate` (line ~1939) feeds `openInputThreads.length` / `replyCoverage.unaddressed.length` (which includes null-id threads) into `evaluateAuditResolveGate`, so `blocked = realCodeChanges === false && openThreadCount > 0 && unaddressedCount > 0` can never be false on a PR whose open threads are all null-id.

**Impact**: On blocked passes (the passes where a human decision is most needed) the actionable message is drowned under the thread dump or missing entirely; PRs whose open threads are all null-id machine notices re-enter the blocked path on every lap — an infinite blocked loop.

**Fix approach** (gh-1061):
- AC1/AC2/AC4: new pure composer `buildBlockedReworkComment` — header line, then the agent's response.md verbatim; unaddressed-thread enumeration moves into a collapsed `<details>` fold (3 previews + "…and N more", compact hard-capped labels, full list inside); missing response.md produces an explicit "agent wrote no response.md — see run log <url>" sentence. Helper `threadShortLabel` keeps the 39-thread body under ~2000 chars.
- AC3: `isUnaddressableThread` (threadKeyOf === null) splits open threads into addressable/unaddressable in `buildReplyCoverage`; the coverage-gate denominator (`openCount`, `unaddressed`) counts addressable threads only; null-id notices are returned as informational `unaddressable` context and reported in the fold.
- AC5: one sentence added to the blocked contract in `instructions/pr_rework/output_rules.md` and mirrored in `prompts/pr_rework_prompt.md`.

**Previous attempt**: not a returned bug — fresh RCA from the ticket description.

/**
 * Machine-notice classification for PR discussion collection (gh-808).
 *
 * The harness posts STATUS/ARMING notices to its own PRs through the machine
 * login — arming notices, park/park-clear notices, validation and re-run
 * reports, merge-conflict reports, rework/review result summaries, human
 * escalations. Those notices are NOT review feedback: feeding them into the
 * rework input as threads with reply targeting made the rework agent spend
 * its replies on boilerplate answers to the machine itself (live: fa PR
 * #1428 round 2 — 9 of 13 replies were boilerplate).
 *
 * This module is the SINGLE SOURCE OF TRUTH for recognizing those notices.
 * The discrimination cannot be authorship-based: in this harness the reviewer
 * identity IS the machine login (the review agent posts inline comments with
 * the same credentials that post the notices), so classification keys on the
 * exact marker each poster writes at the START of its comment body — anchored
 * prefix match, never fuzzy text matching. A reviewer comment that merely
 * QUOTES a notice (blockquote, mid-body mention) therefore never matches.
 *
 * Comment bodies rendered through commentMarkup start with a markdown heading
 * (`### ✅ Rework Completed`), so a leading heading prefix is stripped before
 * the marker comparison.
 *
 * Consumption: js/common/scm.js (GitHub provider fetchDiscussions) and
 * js/common/githubHelpers.js (string-arg fetchDiscussionsAndRawData) drop
 * matching conversations from rawThreads and the discussions markdown, so
 * pr_discussions_raw.json contains zero machine-notice entries (gh-808 AC1)
 * while real review threads pass through with their ids intact (AC2).
 */

// Exact body-start markers of every PR-level notice the harness posts, with
// the poster that owns each. Keep in sync with the posters — when the armer
// wording changes, the marker changes here with it.
var MACHINE_NOTICE_MARKERS = [
    // js/smAgent.js — arm_rework notice
    '🧵 Unresolved review threads — rework armed.',
    // js/smAgent.js — validation park + park-clear notices
    '🅿️ Validation red — PR parked',
    '🅿️→▶ validation_failed cleared',
    // js/smAgent.js — rerun_cancelled_checks notice
    '🔁 Cancelled required checks re-run',
    // js/smAgent.js — conflict_rework report
    '⚠️ Merge conflict with main',
    // js/smAgent.js — fail_validation reports (all wording variants)
    '⚠️ Validation CI went red on the head',
    // js/smAgent.js — guest-PR park notice + human escalation (#701 style)
    '🛑 validation_failed',
    '🛑 @',
    // js/pushReworkChanges.js — rework completion comments (h3 headings)
    '✅ Rework Completed',
    '⚠️ Rework Completed',
    '✅ Rework Analysis Completed',
    // js/pushReworkChanges.js — rework failure reports
    '❌ Rework CLI Failed',
    '❌ Rework Push Skipped',
    '❌ Rework Push Failed',
    '❌ Rework Quality Gate Failed',
    '❌ Rework Workflow Error',
    // js/pushReworkChanges.js — re-review skip notices (token guard)
    '✅ Rework finished.',
    '⚠️ Rework finished with',
    // js/pushReworkChanges.js — fix summary + gate warnings + untargeted replies
    '🔧 Rework Complete —',
    '⚠️ Non-blocking gate warnings',
    '✅ Addressed',
    // js/postPRReviewComments.js — review summary (h2 heading)
    '🔍 Automated PR Review Completed',
    // js/postTestReworkResults.js / js/storyTestAutomationRework.js — test rework summaries
    '🔧 Test Rework Complete —',
    '🔧 Story Test Rework Complete —'
];

// Bot accounts whose PR threads are informational by platform convention

# Copilot Instructions — dmtools-agents

## Architecture

This is a **generic agents repository** (typically used as a git submodule at `agents/` inside product repos). It orchestrates AI-driven Agile delivery via [dmtools](https://github.com/nicku/dmtools) — a Java tool that provides a GraalJS runtime for agent scripts.

### Execution model

1. **SM Agent** (`sm.json` → `js/smAgent.js`) runs on a cron schedule, queries Jira via JQL rules, and dispatches specialized agents by triggering GitHub Actions workflows.
2. **Agent configs** (root `*.json` files) define individual agent jobs. Three job types exist:
   - `Teammate` — CLI-based agent (prepares context → runs AI CLI → post-processes result)
   - `JSRunner` — pure GraalJS logic executed inside dmtools (no AI CLI)
   - `TestCasesGenerator` — dmtools-native job for test case generation
3. **Project config** lives in the target repo at `.dmtools/config.js`, never here. This repo stays project-agnostic.

### Key layers

| Layer | Location | Purpose |
|-------|----------|---------|
| SM rules | `sm.json`, `sm_merge.json` | JQL-based ticket routing |
| Agent configs | root `*.json` | Job definitions (type, params, actions) |
| JS runtime scripts | `js/` | Pre/post actions, orchestration logic |
| Shared helpers | `js/common/` | SCM abstraction, Jira helpers, PR logic |
| Config system | `js/configLoader.js` + `js/config.js` | Discovery, merging, defaults |
| Prompts | `prompts/` | Markdown entry prompts for CLI agents |
| Instructions | `instructions/` | Reusable instruction packs (review, dev, rework, platform, tracker, scm) |
| Setup scripts | `setup/` | Shell scripts for CI environment setup |

## GraalJS Constraints

All `js/` runtime code executes in **dmtools GraalJS**, not Node.js.

- Use `var` declarations and plain functions (no `let`/`const`, no arrow functions, no async/await, no template literals).
- No Node.js APIs: no `fs`, `path`, `process`, `Buffer`, `child_process`, no npm packages.
- No browser APIs: no `fetch`, `window`, `document`.
- Use dmtools globals: `jira_*`, `github_*`, `ado_*`, `file_read`, `file_write`, `cli_execute_command`.
- Local `require('./module.js')` works only for files within this repo.
- **Requires resolve by execution time** (gh-823): a require that runs while a module initializes (top level, top-level `try`/`if`) resolves **file-relative**; a require that runs **after init** (any lazy/deferred call into an exported function) resolves against the **main script's directory — the pack's `js/` root — exclusively**, and a file-relative hit is never tried. `dmtools compile` discovers the pack closure strictly file-relative. Therefore: **hoist every require to the top of the module — never require lazily.** A lazy sibling-flat spec from `js/common/` looks for `js/x.js` and reds the tick ("Failed to require module"), and a pack-root-relative spec (`./common/…`) authored from a nested file fails the pack build. (Worker-source strings are the one exception — they execute on fresh engines and are authored js-root-relative: `require('./common/smProvider.js')`.) The repo-wide pin in `js/unit-tests/test_packRequirePath.js` fails the suite on ANY deferred require in packed code; its `ALLOWED_DEFERRED` list carries exactly one deliberate entry — `writeSolutionAndDiagrams.js`'s cycle-breaking `require('./writeSolutionAndLabels.js')` (hoisting it would close the labels→diagrams cycle at load time) — don't add a second one.
- Keep data structures JSON-safe.

## Running Tests

Tests run **standalone** inside dmtools GraalJS via the custom test runner. The repo is independent — no parent repo or submodule mount needed.

```bash
# Run from the dmtools-agents repo root
cd dmtools-agents

# All tests
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json

# Single test suite
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_smAgent.json
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_configLoader.json
```

Each `run_*.json` specifies which test files to load. Tests use `loadModule()` with mock injection — see `js/unit-tests/testRunner.js` for the framework API (`test()`, `suite()`, `assert.*`, `loadModule()`, `makeRequire()`).

{"content":"# gh-1061 — Root Cause Analysis

## Root Cause Analysis

**Bug**: The blocked-rework PR comment leads with an inline dump of every unaddressed review thread (`threadLabel()` × N, 5070+ chars for the live 39-thread case), burying — or silently omitting — the agent's `outputs/response.md`; and the gh-957 coverage-gate denominator counts threads with no stable id (`threadId` and `rootCommentId` both absent — machine notices such as red-head markers, `rework-consume` payloads, prior blocked comments) that can never receive a targeted reply, making the gate unsatisfiable and the PR blocked-loop forever (live: dmtools-dart PR #420 / gh-395, run 39156398849).

**Root cause**: `js/pushReworkChanges.js`:
1. `handleReworkBlocked` (line ~1498) appends `unaddressed.map(threadLabel).join(', ')` to the visible comment body before the agent's text, and appends the agent's text only when present.
2. `buildReplyCoverage` (line ~631) filters open threads only by `isOpenThread` (resolved/bot) — id-less machine notices stay in the denominator; `runLapGate` (line ~1939) feeds `openInputThreads.length` / `replyCoverage.unaddressed.length` (which includes null-id threads) into `evaluateAuditResolveGate`, so `blocked = realCodeChanges === false && openThreadCount > 0 && unaddressedCount > 0` can never be false on a PR whose open threads are all null-id.

**Impact**: On blocked passes (the passes where a human decision is most needed) the actionable message is drowned under the thread dump or missing entirely; PRs whose open threads are all null-id machine notices re-enter the blocked path on every lap — an infinite blocked loop.

**Fix approach** (gh-1061):
- AC1/AC2/AC4: new pure composer `buildBlockedReworkComment` — header line, then the agent's response.md verbatim; unaddressed-thread enumeration moves into a collapsed `<details>` fold (3 previews + "…and N more", compact hard-capped labels, full list inside); missing response.md produces an explicit "agent wrote no response.md — see run log <url>" sentence. Helper `threadShortLabel` keeps the 39-thread body under ~2000 chars.
- AC3: `isUnaddressableThread` (threadKeyOf === null) splits open threads into addressable/unaddressable in `buildReplyCoverage`; the coverage-gate denominator (`openCount`, `unaddressed`) counts addressable threads only; null-id notices are returned as informational `unaddressable` context and reported in the fold.
- AC5: one sentence added to the blocked contract in `instructions/pr_rework/output_rules.md` and mirrored in `prompts/pr_rework_prompt.md`.

**Previous attempt**: not a returned bug — fresh RCA from the ticket description.

 * its replies on boilerplate answers to the machine itself (live: fa PR
 * #1428 round 2 — 9 of 13 replies were boilerplate).

 * This module is the SINGLE SOURCE OF TRUTH for recognizing those notices.
 * The discrimination cannot be authorship-based: in this harness the reviewer
 * identity IS the machine login (the review agent posts inline comments with
 * the same credentials that post the notices), so classification keys on the
 * exact marker each poster writes at the START of its comment body — anchored
 * prefix match, never fuzzy text matching. A reviewer comment that merely
 * QUOTES a notice (blockquote, mid-body mention) therefore never matches.

# Copilot Instructions — dmtools-agents

## Architecture

This is a **generic agents repository** (typically used as a git submodule at `agents/` inside product repos). It orchestrates AI-driven Agile delivery via [dmtools](https://github.com/nicku/dmtools) — a Java tool that provides a GraalJS runtime for agent scripts.

### Execution model

1. **SM Agent** (`sm.json` → `js/smAgent.js`) runs on a cron schedule, queries Jira via JQL rules, and dispatches specialized agents by triggering GitHub Actions workflows.
2. **Agent configs** (root `*.json` files) define individual agent jobs. Three job types exist:
   - `Teammate` — CLI-based agent (prepares context → runs AI CLI → post-processes result)
   - `JSRunner` — pure GraalJS logic executed inside dmtools (no AI CLI)
   - `TestCasesGenerator` — dmtools-native job for test case generation
3. **Project config** lives in the target repo at `.dmtools/config.js`, never here. This repo stays project-agnostic.

### Key layers

| Layer | Location | Purpose |
|-------|----------|---------|
| SM rules | `sm.json`, `sm_merge.json` | JQL-based ticket routing |
| Agent configs | root `*.json` | Job definitions (type, params, actions) |
| JS runtime scripts | `js/` | Pre/post actions, orchestration logic |
| Shared helpers | `js/common/` | SCM abstraction, Jira helpers, PR logic |
| Config system | `js/configLoader.js` + `js/config.js` | Discovery, merging, defaults |
| Prompts | `prompts/` | Markdown entry prompts for CLI agents |
| Instructions | `instructions/` | Reusable instruction packs (review, dev, rework, platform, tracker, scm) |
| Setup scripts | `setup/` | Shell scripts for CI environment setup |

## GraalJS Constraints

All `js/` runtime code executes in **dmtools GraalJS**, not Node.js.

- Use `var` declarations and plain functions (no `let`/`const`, no arrow functions, no async/await, no template literals).
- No Node.js APIs: no `fs`, `path`, `process`, `Buffer`, `child_process`, no npm packages.
- No browser APIs: no `fetch`, `window`, `document`.
- Use dmtools globals: `jira_*`, `github_*`, `ado_*`, `file_read`, `file_write`, `cli_execute_command`.
- Local `require('./module.js')` works only for files within this repo.
- **Requires resolve by execution time** (gh-823): a require that runs while a module initializes (top level, top-level `try`/`if`) resolves **file-relative**; a require that runs **after init** (any lazy/deferred call into an exported function) resolves against the **main script's directory — the pack's `js/` root — exclusively**, and a file-relative hit is never tried. `dmtools compile` discovers the pack closure strictly file-relative. Therefore: **hoist every require to the top of the module — never require lazily.** A lazy sibling-flat spec from `js/common/` looks for `js/x.js` and reds the tick ("Failed to require module"), and a pack-root-relative spec (`./common/…`) authored from a nested file fails the pack build. (Worker-source strings are the one exception — they execute on fresh engines and are authored js-root-relative: `require('./common/smProvider.js')`.) The repo-wide pin in `js/unit-tests/test_packRequirePath.js` fails the suite on ANY deferred require in packed code; its `ALLOWED_DEFERRED` list carries exactly one deliberate entry — `writeSolutionAndDiagrams.js`'s cycle-breaking `require('./writeSolutionAndLabels.js')` (hoisting it would close the labels→diagrams cycle at load time) — don't add a second one.
- Keep data structures JSON-safe.

## Running Tests

Tests run **standalone** inside dmtools GraalJS via the custom test runner. The repo is independent — no parent repo or submodule mount needed.

```bash
# Run from the dmtools-agents repo root
cd dmtools-agents

# All tests
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json

# Single test suite
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_smAgent.json
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_configLoader.json
```

Each `run_*.json` specifies which test files to load. Tests use `loadModule()` with mock injection — see `js/unit-tests/testRunner.js` for the framework API (`test()`, `suite()`, `assert.*`, `loadModule()`, `makeRequire()`).

{"content":"# gh-1061 — Root Cause Analysis

## Root Cause Analysis

**Bug**: The blocked-rework PR comment leads with an inline dump of every unaddressed review thread (`threadLabel()` × N, 5070+ chars for the live 39-thread case), burying — or silently omitting — the agent's `outputs/response.md`; and the gh-957 coverage-gate denominator counts threads with no stable id (`threadId` and `rootCommentId` both absent — machine notices such as red-head markers, `rework-consume` payloads, prior blocked comments) that can never receive a targeted reply, making the gate unsatisfiable and the PR blocked-loop forever (live: dmtools-dart PR #420 / gh-395, run 39156398849).

**Root cause**: `js/pushReworkChanges.js`:
1. `handleReworkBlocked` (line ~1498) appends `unaddressed.map(threadLabel).join(', ')` to the visible comment body before the agent's text, and appends the agent's text only when present.
2. `buildReplyCoverage` (line ~631) filters open threads only by `isOpenThread` (resolved/bot) — id-less machine notices stay in the denominator; `runLapGate` (line ~1939) feeds `openInputThreads.length` / `replyCoverage.unaddressed.length` (which includes null-id threads) into `evaluateAuditResolveGate`, so `blocked = realCodeChanges === false && openThreadCount > 0 && unaddressedCount > 0` can never be false on a PR whose open threads are all null-id.

**Impact**: On blocked passes (the passes where a human decision is most needed) the actionable message is drowned under the thread dump or missing entirely; PRs whose open threads are all null-id machine notices re-enter the blocked path on every lap — an infinite blocked loop.

**Fix approach** (gh-1061):
- AC1/AC2/AC4: new pure composer `buildBlockedReworkComment` — header line, then the agent's response.md verbatim; unaddressed-thread enumeration moves into a collapsed `<details>` fold (3 previews + "…and N more", compact hard-capped labels, full list inside); missing response.md produces an explicit "agent wrote no response.md — see run log <url>" sentence. Helper `threadShortLabel` keeps the 39-thread body under ~2000 chars.
- AC3: `isUnaddressableThread` (threadKeyOf === null) splits open threads into addressable/unaddressable in `buildReplyCoverage`; the coverage-gate denominator (`openCount`, `unaddressed`) counts addressable threads only; null-id notices are returned as informational `unaddressable` context and reported in the fold.
- AC5: one sentence added to the blocked contract in `instructions/pr_rework/output_rules.md` and mirrored in `prompts/pr_rework_prompt.md`.

**Previous attempt**: not a returned bug — fresh RCA from the ticket description.

Baseline: 115 passed, 0 failed. The stack trace noise is expected test output.

Now let me understand the structure of the fix:

1. **AC3** — Exclude null-threadId threads from the coverage-gate denominator. `buildReplyCoverage` currently counts all `isOpenThread` threads in the denominator, and threads without threadId can never be targeted by reply (well — `replyTargetsThread` can match by rootCommentId actually! Wait: `replyTargetsThread` matches by threadId OR rootCommentId/inReplyToId. A thread with null threadId but a rootCommentId CAN be targeted via rootCommentId. Hmm.

# Copilot Instructions — dmtools-agents

## Architecture

This is a **generic agents repository** (typically used as a git submodule at `agents/` inside product repos). It orchestrates AI-driven Agile delivery via [dmtools](https://github.com/nicku/dmtools) — a Java tool that provides a GraalJS runtime for agent scripts.

### Execution model

1. **SM Agent** (`sm.json` → `js/smAgent.js`) runs on a cron schedule, queries Jira via JQL rules, and dispatches specialized agents by triggering GitHub Actions workflows.
2. **Agent configs** (root `*.json` files) define individual agent jobs. Three job types exist:
   - `Teammate` — CLI-based agent (prepares context → runs AI CLI → post-processes result)
   - `JSRunner` — pure GraalJS logic executed inside dmtools (no AI CLI)
   - `TestCasesGenerator` — dmtools-native job for test case generation
3. **Project config** lives in the target repo at `.dmtools/config.js`, never here. This repo stays project-agnostic.

### Key layers

| Layer | Location | Purpose |
|-------|----------|---------|
| SM rules | `sm.json`, `sm_merge.json` | JQL-based ticket routing |
| Agent configs | root `*.json` | Job definitions (type, params, actions) |
| JS runtime scripts | `js/` | Pre/post actions, orchestration logic |
| Shared helpers | `js/common/` | SCM abstraction, Jira helpers, PR logic |
| Config system | `js/configLoader.js` + `js/config.js` | Discovery, merging, defaults |
| Prompts | `prompts/` | Markdown entry prompts for CLI agents |
| Instructions | `instructions/` | Reusable instruction packs (review, dev, rework, platform, tracker, scm) |
| Setup scripts | `setup/` | Shell scripts for CI environment setup |

## GraalJS Constraints

All `js/` runtime code executes in **dmtools GraalJS**, not Node.js.

- Use `var` declarations and plain functions (no `let`/`const`, no arrow functions, no async/await, no template literals).
- No Node.js APIs: no `fs`, `path`, `process`, `Buffer`, `child_process`, no npm packages.
- No browser APIs: no `fetch`, `window`, `document`.
- Use dmtools globals: `jira_*`, `github_*`, `ado_*`, `file_read`, `file_write`, `cli_execute_command`.
- Local `require('./module.js')` works only for files within this repo.
- **Requires resolve by execution time** (gh-823): a require that runs while a module initializes (top level, top-level `try`/`if`) resolves **file-relative**; a require that runs **after init** (any lazy/deferred call into an exported function) resolves against the **main script's directory — the pack's `js/` root — exclusively**, and a file-relative hit is never tried. `dmtools compile` discovers the pack closure strictly file-relative. Therefore: **hoist every require to the top of the module — never require lazily.** A lazy sibling-flat spec from `js/common/` looks for `js/x.js` and reds the tick ("Failed to require module"), and a pack-root-relative spec (`./common/…`) authored from a nested file fails the pack build. (Worker-source strings are the one exception — they execute on fresh engines and are authored js-root-relative: `require('./common/smProvider.js')`.) The repo-wide pin in `js/unit-tests/test_packRequirePath.js` fails the suite on ANY deferred require in packed code; its `ALLOWED_DEFERRED` list carries exactly one deliberate entry — `writeSolutionAndDiagrams.js`'s cycle-breaking `require('./writeSolutionAndLabels.js')` (hoisting it would close the labels→diagrams cycle at load time) — don't add a second one.
- Keep data structures JSON-safe.

## Running Tests

Tests run **standalone** inside dmtools GraalJS via the custom test runner. The repo is independent — no parent repo or submodule mount needed.

```bash
# Run from the dmtools-agents repo root
cd dmtools-agents

# All tests
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json

# Single test suite
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_smAgent.json
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_configLoader.json
```

Each `run_*.json` specifies which test files to load. Tests use `loadModule()` with mock injection — see `js/unit-tests/testRunner.js` for the framework API (`test()`, `suite()`, `assert.*`, `loadModule()`, `makeRequire()`).

{"content":"# gh-1061 — Root Cause Analysis

## Root Cause Analysis

**Bug**: The blocked-rework PR comment leads with an inline dump of every unaddressed review thread (`threadLabel()` × N, 5070+ chars for the live 39-thread case), burying — or silently omitting — the agent's `outputs/response.md`; and the gh-957 coverage-gate denominator counts threads with no stable id (`threadId` and `rootCommentId` both absent — machine notices such as red-head markers, `rework-consume` payloads, prior blocked comments) that can never receive a targeted reply, making the gate unsatisfiable and the PR blocked-loop forever (live: dmtools-dart PR #420 / gh-395, run 39156398849).

**Root cause**: `js/pushReworkChanges.js`:
1. `handleReworkBlocked` (line ~1498) appends `unaddressed.map(threadLabel).join(', ')` to the visible comment body before the agent's text, and appends the agent's text only when present.
2. `buildReplyCoverage` (line ~631) filters open threads only by `isOpenThread` (resolved/bot) — id-less machine notices stay in the denominator; `runLapGate` (line ~1939) feeds `openInputThreads.length` / `replyCoverage.unaddressed.length` (which includes null-id threads) into `evaluateAuditResolveGate`, so `blocked = realCodeChanges === false && openThreadCount > 0 && unaddressedCount > 0` can never be false on a PR whose open threads are all null-id.

**Impact**: On blocked passes (the passes where a human decision is most needed) the actionable message is drowned under the thread dump or missing entirely; PRs whose open threads are all null-id machine notices re-enter the blocked path on every lap — an infinite blocked loop.

**Fix approach** (gh-1061):
- AC1/AC2/AC4: new pure composer `buildBlockedReworkComment` — header line, then the agent's response.md verbatim; unaddressed-thread enumeration moves into a collapsed `<details>` fold (3 previews + "…and N more", compact hard-capped labels, full list inside); missing response.md produces an explicit "agent wrote no response.md — see run log <url>" sentence. Helper `threadShortLabel` keeps the 39-thread body under ~2000 chars.
- AC3: `isUnaddressableThread` (threadKeyOf === null) splits open threads into addressable/unaddressable in `buildReplyCoverage`; the coverage-gate denominator (`openCount`, `unaddressed`) counts addressable threads only; null-id notices are returned as informational `unaddressable` context and reported in the fold.
- AC5: one sentence added to the blocked contract in `instructions/pr_rework/output_rules.md` and mirrored in `prompts/pr_rework_prompt.md`.

**Previous attempt**: not a returned bug — fresh RCA from the ticket description.

/**
 * Machine-notice classification for PR discussion collection (gh-808).
 *
 * The harness posts STATUS/ARMING notices to its own PRs through the machine
 * login — arming notices, park/park-clear notices, validation and re-run
 * reports, merge-conflict reports, rework/review result summaries, human
 * escalations. Those notices are NOT review feedback: feeding them into the
 * rework input as threads with reply targeting made the rework agent spend
 * its replies on boilerplate answers to the machine itself (live: fa PR
 * #1428 round 2 — 9 of 13 replies were boilerplate).
 *
 * This module is the SINGLE SOURCE OF TRUTH for recognizing those notices.
 * The discrimination cannot be authorship-based: in this harness the reviewer
 * identity IS the machine login (the review agent posts inline comments with
 * the same credentials that post the notices), so classification keys on the
 * exact marker each poster writes at the START of its comment body — anchored
 * prefix match, never fuzzy text matching. A reviewer comment that merely
 * QUOTES a notice (blockquote, mid-body mention) therefore never matches.
 *
 * Comment bodies rendered through commentMarkup start with a markdown heading
 * (`### ✅ Rework Completed`), so a leading heading prefix is stripped before
 * the marker comparison.
 *
 * Consumption: js/common/scm.js (GitHub provider fetchDiscussions) and
 * js/common/githubHelpers.js (string-arg fetchDiscussionsAndRawData) drop
 * matching conversations from rawThreads and the discussions markdown, so
 * pr_discussions_raw.json contains zero machine-notice entries (gh-808 AC1)
 * while real review threads pass through with their ids intact (AC2).

// the poster that owns each. Keep in sync with the posters — when the armer

    // js/smAgent.js — arm_rework notice
